hr_012:n1.prompt:
You are helping me research and compare 401(k) providers for my company so I can make an informed final selection myself. I have not yet decided on a provider.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) my company domain/name and state(s) where employees are located (to confirm state-mandate requirements, e.g. CalSavers exemptions), (2) approximate employee headcount, (3) whether I already use a payroll provider (name it) since payroll integration compatibility matters, and (4) any budget constraints or preferences (e.g., low admin fees vs. full-service support).

Then research and build a comparison table of at least 4-5 well-known 401(k) providers commonly used by small/mid-size startups (such as Guideline, Human Interest, Betterment for Business, ADP, Vestwell, or similar). For each provider, gather and tabulate: monthly/annual admin fees, per-employee fees, fund menu breadth and expense ratios, whether they support employer matching structures, payroll integrations they natively support (especially with my stated payroll provider), automatic state-mandate compliance features, ease of plan adoption/setup, and customer support reputation (cite sources).

Present this as a clear side-by-side table plus a short written summary of tradeoffs (e.g., cheapest vs. best integration vs. best fund selection). Do not rank or recommend a single "winner" as the definitive choice — instead highlight 2-3 top contenders based on my stated priorities and explain the reasoning so I can decide.

Once the comparison is ready, stop for human sign-off — I will personally review the table and make the final provider selection; do not sign up, submit applications, or commit to any provider on my behalf.

Report back with the comparison table, sources/links used, and your shortlisted 2-3 contenders with reasoning.

hr_012:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a decision packet for our company's 401(k) employer match and eligibility rules. This is a compensation-policy decision that only company leadership can finalize, so your job is to research, model, and draft options — not to decide or submit anything.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: our current headcount, average/median salary, monthly payroll cost, budget range we're considering for retirement benefits, our state (since match/eligibility rules interact with state-mandated retirement laws like California's), and any existing eligibility norms (e.g., waiting periods, minimum hours, part-time inclusion).

Then produce a written comparison covering at least these employer match structures: no match with auto-enrollment only, a flat percentage match (e.g., 3% of salary), a partial match with cap (e.g., 50% up to 6%), and a tiered/graduated match. For each, estimate annual employer cost using our payroll figures, note pros/cons for retention and recruiting, and flag compliance considerations (e.g., safe harbor status, nondiscrimination testing implications).

Also draft eligibility rule options: immediate eligibility vs. a waiting period (e.g., 30/60/90 days), minimum age, minimum hours-per-week thresholds, and treatment of part-time/seasonal workers, noting how each interacts with state-mandate requirements if applicable.

Organize everything into a clear one-page decision memo with a recommendation section left blank (or with your suggested option clearly labeled as a suggestion only) for leadership to choose from.

When the memo is ready, report back with the full draft, the cost estimates, and a short list of open questions leadership must answer. Do not finalize, adopt, or communicate any match or eligibility policy — this must stop for human sign-off.

hr_012:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT execute) the signing of our company's 401(k) plan adoption agreement. This is a fiduciary act under ERISA that must be signed by an authorized officer of the company — signing itself remains a human step and you must not sign, click accept, submit, or otherwise execute the agreement on my behalf.

Please do the following preparatory work:
1. Ask me for: the name of the 401(k) provider/recordkeeper we selected, the login/portal URL (if any) where the plan adoption agreement is generated or hosted, the finalized plan design decisions (eligibility rules, vesting schedule, employer match formula, effective date), and the name/title of the authorized signing officer.
2. If the provider's portal is accessible with my configured credentials, log in and navigate to the plan adoption agreement or plan document section, and pull up or download the current draft for review — do not submit or sign it.
3. Review the draft against the plan design decisions I gave you and flag any discrepancies, missing fields, blank signature blocks, or inconsistencies (e.g., match formula, eligibility waiting period, vesting schedule) in a clear summary.
4. Prepare a concise checklist for the signing officer: what to verify, what to double-check against payroll/HR records, and where in the portal or document the signature field is located.
5. Compile all of this — draft link/location, discrepancy notes, and the sign-off checklist — into one summary.

When done, report back with: the provider name, a link or file reference to the draft agreement, your discrepancy findings, and the prepared checklist. Then stop for human sign-off — the authorized officer must review and execute the signature themselves.

hr_012:n4.prompt:
You are helping me connect our new 401(k) retirement plan to our payroll system so contributions sync automatically each pay cycle. Our payroll provider is {{vendor}}.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in our workspace or configured credentials:
- The name/plan ID of our adopted 401(k) plan and the recordkeeper or TPA it's set up with
- The employee deferral elections and employer match formula we've decided on
- Confirmation of which {{vendor}} account/company ID to use if we have more than one
- Effective date the deduction should start

Then do the following:
1. Using your configured credentials, sign in to {{vendor}} (via its dashboard or documented API) and locate the benefits/deductions configuration area.
2. Create the 401(k) deduction/benefit item in {{vendor}}, entering the employer match formula, employee deferral setup, and effective date I provided.
3. If {{vendor}} supports webhooks for payroll lifecycle events (payroll processed, employee onboarded, payment failed), subscribe to or verify subscription to these events so we can monitor sync status and catch failures automatically.
4. Confirm the integration links to the correct plan/recordkeeper record so contribution amounts will route correctly.
5. Run a validation check (test payroll run, sandbox mode, or {{vendor}}'s built-in preview if available) to confirm the deduction calculates correctly for at least one sample employee before it goes live on real payroll.

What done looks like: the 401(k) deduction/benefit is fully configured in {{vendor}}, linked to our plan, webhook subscriptions (if supported) are active, and a test calculation confirms correct employee and employer contribution amounts.

Report back to me with: what was configured, any webhook subscriptions created, the test/validation results, and any errors, missing permissions, or setup steps that require my input or the plan provider's confirmation before the first live contribution.

hr_012:n5.prompt:
You are helping me announce our new 401(k) retirement plan enrollment to the team via {{vendor}}, our team-chat tool. The plan is already set up (provider selected, match decided, adoption agreement signed, payroll connected). This step is just the internal announcement.

Before you start, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials, such as: the {{vendor}} channel name to post in (e.g. #general or #hr-announcements), the plan provider name, the employer match details, the enrollment deadline or start date, and any enrollment portal link or instructions employees should follow.

Once you have that information:
1. Draft a clear, friendly announcement message covering: that a 401(k) plan is now available, the provider name, the match policy, how/where to enroll, the enrollment deadline, and a contact (me, or HR) for questions.
2. Show me the draft message for review before posting.
3. After I confirm the wording, post the message to the specified {{vendor}} channel using send_message via the configured API/webhook access.
4. If {{vendor}} supports threads, note that you can use a thread for follow-up questions so replies stay attached to the original announcement.
5. Confirm the message posted successfully by checking for a success response or confirmation from the API/webhook call.

Done looks like: the announcement message has been posted to the correct channel in {{vendor}}, is accurate (correct provider, match, deadline, enrollment link), and you have confirmation it sent successfully (e.g., a message ID or timestamp returned by the API).

Report back to me with: the final text of the message you posted, the channel it was posted to, the timestamp/confirmation of successful posting, and any errors or issues encountered (e.g., missing permissions, invalid channel, webhook failure) so I can resolve them.

hr_012:n6.prompt:
You are helping me verify that the first 401(k) contribution from our payroll system has correctly synced to our retirement plan provider. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) the name of our payroll provider (e.g., Gusto, Rippling, ADP), (b) the name of our 401(k) plan provider, (c) the pay date of the first payroll run that should include 401(k) deductions, and (d) which employees were enrolled and their expected contribution amounts/percentages (I can paste a list or point you to where it's stored).

2. Using my configured credentials, log into the payroll system's dashboard and confirm the 401(k) deduction line items appear correctly on the relevant pay run — check that amounts match each employee's elected contribution rate and that any employer match is calculated per our plan's match formula.

3. Log into the 401(k) plan provider's dashboard using my configured credentials and check whether the contribution file/report for that pay date has been received and posted — confirm the total dollar amount and per-employee breakdown match what payroll withheld.

4. Flag any discrepancies: missing employees, mismatched dollar amounts, missing employer match, or a contribution file that shows as "pending" or "failed" on the provider side.

5. If the integration between payroll and the provider is API/feed-based, check the integration status or sync log in either dashboard for error messages.

Done looks like: you can confirm (or clearly report a discrepancy in) whether the contribution amounts withheld in payroll match what was received and posted by the plan provider for the first pay cycle, including employer match if applicable.

Report back with: a summary table of employee, expected contribution, payroll-reported amount, provider-received amount, and match status (OK/mismatch/pending), plus any error messages found. Do not attempt to fix payroll settings or resubmit contributions yourself — if a mismatch exists, prepare a clear summary of the issue for me to resolve, since correcting live payroll deduction settings remains a human step.
